items.title: Candido Camero — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee mentions Chano Pozo as the director of a comparsa in his neighborhood and a composer, but does not describe a direct personal, professional, or collaborative relationship between himself and Chano Pozo.

ctx.x: You tell me that in Cuba there are forty-three neighborhoods. That reminds me of the carnivals.

(Laughs) In fact I was going to tell you about that. Each neighborhood has its comparsa. But not because I'm from El Cerro but in the Traditional category, my neighborhood’s comparsa, Los Alacranes (The Scorpions), always took the first prize in the Traditional category. Now the comparsa in the neighborhood of Belén, whose director was Chano Pozo, they always took first prize in Elegance. Los Dandys de Belén always took the first prize. The director was Chano Pozo. They always took the first prize in Elegance. El…
For a person who is not Cuban who has not lived that time, describe the celebration, the parade, those carnivals. Each neighborhood came marching with its troupe towards one meeting place?
